key_insight: MSVR lets optimization algorithms track many coupled component functions with only O(1) stochastic probes per iteration, enabling efficient variance reduction for finite-sum compositional problems.
engineering_relevance: This is useful for large-scale machine learning and scientific optimization settings where memory, sampling, or oracle access is limited but many coupled blocks must be updated reliably.
method: Introduces a Multi-block-Single-probe Variance Reduction (MSVR) estimator to track \(\mathbf g(\mathbf w)=(g_1,\dots,g_m)\) under partial block sampling.
Builds FCCO algorithms on top of MSVR and analyzes convergence for non-convex, convex, strongly convex, and PL objectives.
Exploits a special linear-gradient case to reduce dependence on \(m\) in the sample complexity.
evidence_signal: The abstract reports improved sample-complexity guarantees across multiple objective classes and stronger performance in multi-task deep AUC maximization experiments.
watch_item: Performance depends on stochastic oracle access and block-sampling design, so practical gains may vary with probe budget and the cost of evaluating selected blocks.
paper_title: Solving Finite-sum Coupled Compositional Optimization via Multi-block-Single-probe Estimator
